summary: Pre-market, the composite risk score eased to 41.95 (caution / goldilocks), with the 1-day trend at -0.58 and the 1-week trend at -1.14; all 7 datasets are fresh. Overnight the story was rates, not risk appetite: global bond yields are at multi-decade highs amid the US-Iran stalemate - the ten-year yield backed up to 4.68 and the real rate sits at 2.41 (98.23 percentile), keeping macro the binding constraint (dimension 60.57) - yet VIX fell to 14.25, HY OAS tightened to 2.67 and the dollar eased to 118.90, with disinflation intact (CPI 3.30, core 2.47, PCE 3.29). The memory supercycle kept dividing markets: GigaDevice's half-year net profit surged 1091.5% (top headline), but the A-share chain faded at the China close (ChangXin -4.22, GigaDevice -1.64, Longsys -1.69) while Micron held +2.30 and AMD +6.50. Breadth remains narrow - 73.55% above the 200-day but only 4.52% at new highs. Baidu reported below estimates this morning; Target, Walmart and Alibaba follow, and Nvidia reports late next week.

top_risk_drivers.claim: Macro remains the binding constraint: the real rate at 2.41 sits at the 98.23 percentile and the ten-year yield backed up to 4.68 (97.51 percentile), holding the macro dimension at 60.57 - the largest structural risk even as volatility falls and credit stays tight.

Cross-asset confirmation (0.5714) is again the largest single contributor at 7.50 - but it is a proxy (discounted 0.8), and with dollar strength and real-rate pressure both triggered, the hard-signal read is mixed.

The memory supercycle is bifurcating: GigaDevice's half-year net profit jumped 1091.5% (the top news item), yet the A-share chain faded at the China close (ChangXin -4.22, GigaDevice -1.64, Longsys -1.69) after Monday's surge, while Micron added 2.30 and AMD 6.50 overnight.
Breadth is fractured: 73.55% of names sit above their 200-day, but the new-highs ratio is just 4.52% (7 of 155) - the rally is a narrow, memory-led tape.

The AI-capex financing engine is the overnight theme: Nvidia is backing massive financing for an OpenAI data center in Ohio, following SEC guidance that takes sponsors off the hook for data-center bonds.

supporting_signals.claim: Disinflation is intact - CPI 3.30 (prior 3.46), core 2.47 (prior 2.57), PCE 3.29 (prior 3.42) - supporting the Fed's hold (implied rate 3.67).
Volatility and credit are calm: VIX fell to 14.25 and HY OAS tightened to 2.67, while breadth holds at 73.55% above the 200-day - the regime reads goldilocks.
The dollar eased to 118.90 (down from 119.18) even as global yields rose, and the memory upcycle is translating into earnings - GigaDevice's half-year net profit up 1091.5%.

contradicting_signals.claim: Against the falling composite score, yields are backing up - the ten-year rose to 4.68 (from 4.63), the real rate to 2.41 (from 2.39) - and the headline risk is 'global bond yields at multi-decade highs' on the US-Iran stalemate.

The A-share memory chain reversed at the close (ChangXin -4.22, GigaDevice -1.64, Longsys -1.69) despite record earnings, and software/cloud themes lagged hard overnight (cybersecurity -2.54, cloud -2.11, AI software -1.77).

what_changed_today: The composite risk score eased to 41.95 (day -0.58, week -1.14) with all 7 datasets fresh.
GigaDevice reported half-year net profit up 1091.5%, the top China-market headline of the session.
Baidu reported second-quarter results this morning, with adjusted per-ADS profit of 7.22 yuan below the 9.75 yuan estimate.
watch_next: Today: Baidu reported before the open; the US session brings global-yield stress and data-center-financing headlines into focus.
Target reports tomorrow (8/19) and Walmart plus Alibaba on Thursday (8/20) - a heavy US retail tape to test the consumer.
Zoom on 8/25 and Nvidia on 8/26, with GDP and personal income the same day - the heavyweight window of the week.
Watch whether the A-share memory chain stabilizes after today's fade - GigaDevice's 1091.5% profit growth keeps the fundamental engine intact.

bull_case.title: Memory supercycle carries the tape
points: The memory upcycle is delivering earnings - GigaDevice +1091.5% half-year net profit - while Micron (2.30 overnight, +10.72 on the week) and AMD (+6.50) keep the US semis complex bid.
Disinflation (CPI 3.30, core 2.47, PCE 3.29) plus a falling VIX (14.25) and tight credit (HY OAS 2.67) keep the goldilocks regime intact.
The AI-capex financing engine keeps scaling - Nvidia's Ohio data-center backing and continued memory capex support the hardware complex.

base_case.title: Rates cap the upside; grind sideways
points: Macro stays the binding constraint (real rate 2.41 at the 98.23 percentile), so multiple expansion is capped while earnings carry the market.
Breadth stays narrow (new-highs ratio 4.52%) - leadership remains concentrated in a few memory and AI names.
The calendar is heavy but mostly medium-importance until Nvidia on 8/26; expect range-bound trading into next week.

bear_case.title: Rates break higher and breadth cracks
points: If global yields keep climbing on the US-Iran stalemate, the real rate at 2.41 (98.23 percentile) tightens financial conditions into a fragile breadth tape.
The memory trade is crowded - the A-share chain already faded today (-4.22 ChangXin, -1.64 GigaDevice, -1.69 Longsys) - and an unwind could hit both markets.
Labor cracks persist (payrolls -23.0, participation 61.4) - if next week's GDP and personal income confirm a slowdown, the consumer-exposed rally loses support.
